Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 88, English)
First Mool Tatva Session After Mahotsav: Aura-Checking Results, the Continuous Havan, and a New Navratri Mantra Shakti Sadhna

This session is the first "Mool T atva" session held after a 20-day Mahotsav (annual gathering/festival), opening with aurachecking r esults and r eflections on Mahotsav , then transitioning into the announcement and detailed Q&A for a new Navratri sadhna designed to str engthen practitioners' mantra shakti and mantra doot. Standar d number ed format is used given the substantial teaching and extensive live Q&A content.

1. Opening: First Mool Tatva Session and Aura-Checking After Mahotsav Bhaiya opens by noting this is the first Mool Tatva session and the first aura-checking since Mahotsav concluded, and that this aura-checking was both appropriate and necessary to do at this point.

2. Aura-Checking Results: Over 90% Found Well Bhaiya reports that more than 90% of those checked were found to be well, crediting this to guru's grace and to the power of the Jai Siyaram mantra, expressing that such results bring him great joy as evidence of his guru's influence.

3. Reflection: Mahotsav's Twenty Days Passed Quickly Bhaiya reflects that the 20-day Mahotsav passed so quickly it barely felt real; when he asked his guru about extending it further , he was told that the underlying practice had actually already been running for about 45 days by that point.

4. The Continuous (24-Hour) Havan Bhaiya reveals that a havan has been running nearly continuously — close to 24 hours a day — for over 45 days at this point, sustained by dif ferent individuals taking turns in devotion to the guru, without a single point of complete stoppage.

5. Teaching: Why a Collective Effort Doesn't Stop Bhaiya explains that if this continuous havan depended on any single person, it would eventually stop; but because it belongs to everyone collectively , with multiple people ready to take over whenever one pauses, it does not stop — of fered as proof that his vow of a round-the-clock Ram Naam yagna is being fulfilled through the sangat's collective devotion, not through any one individual's ef fort.

6. Reflections and Testimonies on Mahotsav's Emotional Impact Several sangat members shared that leaving Mahotsav was emotionally dif ficult — some described crying while departing, losing track of ordinary time (day/evening/night) during the event, missing the food and treats, and experiencing a kind of "hangover" from the festival's atmosphere afterward.

7. Teaching: What Mahotsav-Style Gatherings Pr ovide Bhaiya explains that the joy of such an annual gathering comes from family sitting together , casual conversation, singing bhajans, seeing (darshan) the divine, and praising the divine's powers in one unified voice — framed as a rare, especially valuable form of collective devotion.

8. Teaching: Prabhu Gave According to Each Person's Need Bhaiya describes that during Mahotsav , the divine gave generously and specifically to each attendee's need — freeing those with negativity from negativity , freeing those with pitru (ancestor) influence from pitru bondage, releasing those bound by tantric practices, granting drishti (vision) to those needing it, granting shakti to those needing
power , granting buddhi (wisdom) and tej (radiance) as needed — and, ultimately , granting everyone the blessing of bhakti (devotion) itself.

9. Teaching: "Sharing Multiplies" (Baantne Se Hi Badhega) Bhaiya teaches that sharing is what causes growth — when a person prays and works for the benefit of others rather than only themselves, that which "belongs to everyone" flows toward the whole group, and this collective orientation is what allows the continuous 24-hour yagna and Ashaeiynn's overall growth to continue.

10. Announcement: A New Navratri Sadhna to Str engthen Mantra Shakti Bhaiya announces a new sadhna to be undertaken during the upcoming Navratri, explicitly clarifying that this is not a Siya Tattva Sadhna and does not carry strict dietary restrictions — practitioners may eat somewhat more at one meal and somewhat less at another , without rigid food or lifestyle prohibitions.

1 1. Origin of This Sadhna: Weak Mantra Shakti Observed in Third Eye Batches Bhaiya explains that this sadhna's design originated from his own observation, during personal Third Eye batch sessions, that many practitioners had fully open chakras and functioning drishti, yet weak underlying mantra shakti — meaning the ener gy behind their drishti wasn't fully operating. He prayed about this (and admits he had actually for gotten the prayer himself), and his guru — who does not for get — later revealed this sadhna as the response.

12. Practice Details: A 40-Minute Daily Sadhna The prescribed practice is a 40-minute sitting session per day , structured as roughly 5 minutes at the start, 25 minutes as the main body , and 5 minutes at the end. Bhaiya emphasizes that 40 minutes is "more than enough," and that during this session ener gy will be sent from the source at an intensity described as 10 to the power of 8 (10^8) times normal, which each practitioner absorbs according to their own body/capacity .

13. Mechanism: How This Sadhna Builds Mantra Doot Bhaiya explains that the ener gy absorbed during this sadhna combines with each practitioner's own mantra to form mantra doot suited to that individual's own body/tattva — meaning mantra shakti is the essential ingredient required to generate mantra doot, and this sadhna's focus is specifically on building that underlying mantra shakti.

14. Practical Gr oup Timing The group session timing is set for after 9:30 p.m., described as a favorable time; those with prior commitments (e.g., evening social events, garba) are advised to complete their 40-minute sadhna first before attending other plans, or may perform the sadhna independently at any convenient time if they cannot join the live group session.

15. Guidance: Suspend Other Personal Practices Ashaeiynn-Specific, But Not All Rituals Bhaiya instructs that during these nine days, practitioners should pause other Ashaeiynn-specific jaap/sadhna routines (e.g., a regular two-hour daily jaap) in favor of this 40minute practice, but personal akhand deepak lighting may continue unaf fected; this pause applies specifically to structured Ashaeiynn practices, not to all religious activity broadly .

16. Q&A: Applicability for Those With Pitru or Negativity Issues In response to a question, Bhaiya confirms that practitioners dealing with pitru-related issues can still do this sadhna, since it works purely on strengthening mantra shakti rather than on pitru/negativity concerns directly .

17. Q&A: Combining With an Ongoing Nine-Day Kalash or Other Sadhna Bhaiya confirms that practitioners maintaining a traditional nine-day Navratri kalash, or already engaged in another ongoing sadhna (e.g., a 21-day sadhna), can perform this mantrashakti sadhna in parallel without disrupting either practice, since this sadhna works purely to increase mantra strength and does not interfere with unrelated practices.

18. Q&A: Sankalp (V ow) Timing and Attendance The formal sankalp for this sadhna will be taken on the first day (a Monday), of fered twice — once in the morning and once in the evening — so practitioners following either schedule can attend the corresponding sankalp session; attending both is welcomed but not required.

19. Q&A: Missing the Sankalp Due to Technical Issues If a practitioner is unable to attend either sankalp session due to a technical dif ficulty or other unavoidable reason, Bhaiya states they can have mentors administer the sankalp to them separately , provided they report the issue on the same day it occurs.

20. Q&A: Extra Jaap Beyond the Pr escribed 40 Minutes Bhaiya confirms extra jaap beyond the prescribed 40-minute session causes no harm and is permitted for those who wish to do more, while cautioning that excessive prolonged mantra jaap (citing examples of seven-to-eight-hour continuous sessions) can cause bodily agitation or unease ("ghabrahat"), so practitioners should proceed only if they feel capable of handling the increased ener gy .
21. Q&A: Continuing the 1 1-Diya Practice Practitioners who regularly perform an 1 1-diya practice may continue doing so alongside this sadhna without conflict.

22. Q&A: Doing the Sadhna While Traveling or Away Fr om Home Bhaiya confirms this sadhna can be performed while traveling or staying elsewhere (e.g., at a wedding function, in a hotel room), as long as the practitioner finds a reasonably suitable space to sit; those who already hold gehan tattva (a prior initiation granting continuous access) are noted as likely to have an especially good experience with this practice regardless of location.

23. Q&A: Performing Devi Path (Scriptur e Recitation) Alongside This Sadhna Bhaiya confirms that practitioners wishing to additionally recite a Devi path (such as during Navratri) may do so, of fered as a witness/independent practice, without conflict.

24. Guidance for Women During Menstrual Impurity Around Sankalp Day Bhaiya gives detailed, sensitive guidance for women whose menstrual cycle may fall around the sankalp date: if a practitioner is in a state of ritual purity on the specific day the sankalp is taken, she may take the sankalp normally , and remains included in it even if her cycle begins one or two days afterward. If, however , a practitioner is in a state of impurity precisely on the sankalp day itself, Bhaiya suggests she consider taking gehan tattva beforehand — since gehan tattva grants two doot enabling jaap access even during periods of ritual impurity — and without gehan tattva, he recommends she not attempt to take the sankalp on that specific day , to avoid unwanted spiritual exposure.

25. Clarification: No "First-Thr ee-Days" Exception Applies Here In response to a question referencing the Siya Tattva Sadhna's policy of allowing late joiners within the first three days to still be included in the sankalp, Bhaiya clarifies that this specific sadhna has no such exception — only the actual sankalp day itself determines a practitioner's inclusion, and this practice's guiding saints/tattva are distinct from those of Siya Tattva Sadhna (which, Bhaiya notes, this time specifically declined to participate, prompting the venue/focus to shift for this sadhna).

26. Announcement: Akhand Deepak Options During This Period Practitioners wishing to light an akhand deepak — whether for their kuldevi (family goddess), a general Navratri deepak, or another dedicated purpose — may do so through Ashaeiynn, all at the same registration amount regardless of purpose; advance booking/registration is required so mentors can prepare properly , since limited time means late requests may need to be turned away in fairness to those who registered on time.

27. Extended Teaching: Why Those With a Kuldevi Should Light an Akhand Deepak Bhaiya teaches that anyone whose family deity (kuldevi) is a form of the goddess incurs a spiritual obligation ("dosh," or fault) if they neglect to honor her during this particularly potent Navratri period — either by lighting an akhand deepak themselves at home or arranging one through Ashaeiynn — drawing a parallel to how neglecting to honor one's own kuldevta during that deity's special period (as Bhaiya does for his own kuldevta, Rama Sarkar , during Mahotsav) would incur the same kind of fault on the descendant.

28. Teaching: The "Equality" Metaphor — Different Families, Differ ent Obligations Using an extended anecdote about two friends with dif ferent household curfew rules (one strict, one lenient) despite being otherwise equal, Bhaiya illustrates that spiritual obligations dif fer by lineage/family deity rather than being uniformly "equal" across all practitioners — encouraging practitioners not to expect identical treatment across dif ferent family deities, since "no two fingers on a hand are equal," and each person's obligation is specific to their own kul (lineage).
29. Guidance for Those Who Don't Know Their Kuldevi/Kuldevta Practitioners unsure of their family deity are invited to fill out a form, after which Ashaeiynn will identify and inform them.

30. Teaching: How Incr eased Mantra Shakti Is Used Is the Practitioner's Choice Bhaiya teaches that once mantra shakti increases through this sadhna, how a practitioner applies that strength is entirely up to them — used for good, it returns good; used for harm, it
eventually returns harm, since "what goes around comes around," and truth ultimately surfaces regardless of delay .

31. Closing: Futur e Mool Tatva Topics Bhaiya notes that previous Mool Tatva sessions have already covered the concept of the universe, Mahashiv , Vishnu tattva, and Ram tattva, with further topics planned for future sessions once current sadhna-related questions are addressed.

32. Closing Reflection: Sadhna Costs Trending Toward Minimal Over Time Bhaiya reflects that as the community has grown, per - person sadhna costs have generally decreased (since costs are shared across more participants), and he expects this trend to continue toward making sadhnas as accessible/minimal-cost as possible so more people can participate; he separately reiterates an open invitation for dedicated practitioners to come learn havan directly and perform it at Ashaeiynn with materials (dry fruits, oil, ghee) provided free of char ge.

33. Closing Blessing and Logistics Bhaiya closes with a blessing for the sangat to remain worry-free, prepare for the sadhna with a light and joyful mindset, and notes that full practical details will be shared through the app and the group.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This aura-checking round (the first since Mahotsav) found more than 90% of practitioners well. A continuous, nearly round-the-clock havan has run for over 45 days as of this session, sustained collectively by many practitioners taking turns rather than any single individual. The new Navratri sadhna announced in this session is specifically designed to increase mantra shakti and build mantra doot — it is not a Siya Tattva Sadhna and carries no strict dietary restrictions. The practice is a 40-minute daily sitting (roughly 5+25+5 minutes), with ener gy sent at 10^8 intensity during group sessions; 40 minutes is described as more than suf ficient, and excessive additional jaap risks bodily agitation. This sadhna can be combined with an ongoing nine-day kalash, another parallel sadhna, travel, or a Devi path recitation, since it works purely on mantra shakti and does not conflict with other practices. Women should take the sankalp only if ritually pure on the specific sankalp day itself; if impure on that day and without gehan tattva, it is recommended not to take the sankalp that day . There is no "first three days" late-inclusion exception for this specific sadhna. Anyone whose kuldevi (family goddess) is a goddess form is encouraged to light an akhand deepak during this Navratri period, either at home or via Ashaeiynn, to avoid incurring spiritual "dosh" from neglecting the family deity during her potent period; advance registration is required for Ashaeiynn-lit deepaks. How increased mantra shakti is subsequently used is the practitioner's own responsibility — used well, it returns well; used poorly , consequences eventually surface. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .

User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn Mool T atva session held after Mahotsav , announcing a new Navratri sadhna focused on mantra shakti.

Q1. What wer e the results of the first aura-checking r ound held after Mahotsav? A: Per this teaching, more than 90% of those checked were found to be well, which Bhaiya credits to guru's grace and the power of the Jai Siyaram mantra.

Q2. How long had the continuous havan actually been running by the time of this session? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya reveals the havan had been running nearly continuously — close to 24 hours a day — for over 45 days by this point, sustained by dif ferent practitioners taking turns.

A: Per this teaching, if the havan depended on any one individual it would eventually stop; but because it belongs to the whole collective, with multiple people ready to take over at any time, it continues without interruption.

Q4. What did Prabhu give to differ ent attendees during Mahotsav , per this teaching? Q5. What does this teaching mean by "sharing multiplies" (baantne se hi badhega)? A: Per this teaching, praying and acting for others' benefit rather than only one's own causes what "belongs to everyone" to keep flowing toward the collective, which Bhaiya identifies as the reason the continuous yagna and Ashaeiynn's overall growth continue.

Q6. What is the purpose of the new Navratri sadhna announced in this session? A: Per this teaching, this new sadhna is specifically designed to increase practitioners' mantra shakti and to build mantra doot; it is explicitly not a Siya Tattva Sadhna and does not carry strict dietary restrictions.

Q9. At what intensity is energy sent during this sadhna's gr oup sessions? A: Per this teaching, ener gy is sent at an intensity described as 10 to the power of 8 (10^8) times normal during group sessions, absorbed by each practitioner according to their own body/capacity .

Q10. How does this sadhna actually build mantra doot? Q1 1. What is the gr oup session timing for this sadhna, and what if a practitioner has a conflicting commitment? A: Per this teaching, the group session timing is set for after 9:30 p.m.; those with prior evening commitments are advised to complete their 40minute sadhna first, or may perform it independently at a convenient time if unable to join the live group session.

Q12. Should practitioners pause their other regular Ashaeiynn practices during these nine days? A: Per this teaching, yes — other structured Ashaeiynn-specific practices (such as a regular two-hour daily jaap) should be paused in favor of this 40-minute sadhna, though a personal akhand deepak may continue unaf fected.

Q13. Can practitioners dealing with pitru-r elated issues do this sadhna? A: Yes — per this teaching, this sadhna works purely on strengthening mantra shakti, so it remains applicable even for practitioners currently dealing with pitru-related issues.

Q14. Can this sadhna be combined with an ongoing nine-day kalash or another parallel sadhna? A: Yes — per this teaching, this sadhna works purely to increase mantra strength and does not interfere with a traditional Navratri kalash or another ongoing sadhna (such as a 21-day sadhna), so it can be performed in parallel.

Q15. When is the formal sankalp for this sadhna held, and is attending both sessions r equired? A: Per this teaching, the sankalp is held on the first day (a Monday), of fered once in the morning and once in the evening for practitioners on dif ferent schedules; attending one session is suf ficient, though attending both is welcomed.

Q16. What should a practitioner do if a technical issue pr events them fr om attending either sankalp session? A: Per this teaching, a practitioner who misses both sankalp sessions due to a technical or other unavoidable issue can have mentors administer the sankalp to them separately , provided they report the issue on the same day .

Q17. Is extra jaap beyond the 40-minute session allowed, and is it advisable? A: Per this teaching, extra jaap is allowed and causes no harm, but practitioners are cautioned that excessive prolonged mantra jaap (citing seven-to-eight-hour continuous sessions as an example) can cause bodily agitation, so extra practice should only be undertaken if the practitioner feels capable of handling the added ener gy .

A: Per this teaching, how a practitioner applies their increased mantra shakti is entirely their own responsibility — used for good, it returns good; used for harm, consequences eventually surface, since "what goes around comes around."
Bot Response Guidelines

Present Q6–Q26 (the new sadhna's rules, timing, and exceptions) as specific, time-bound guidance tied to this particular Navratri sadhna — not as general or permanent rules applicable to all future sadhnas. Present the menstrual-purity guidance (Q21) with care and respect, as this tradition's own specific ritual framework, without generalizing it into broader claims about menstruation. Present the kuldevi/akhand deepak obligation teaching (Q24–Q25) as this tradition's own specific doctrinal framing tied to lineage-based practice, not as a universal claim that applies outside this context. Part III — Curated Conversational Q&A (Hinglish)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Supplement (Session 88, Hinglish)
Mahotsav ke Baad ka Mool Tatva Session aur Navratri Mantra Shakti Sadhna

Note: yeh session mein genuine live back-and-forth substantial thi — Mahotsav ki yaadein, aur nayi sadhna ke rules ke baar e mein bahut sar e practical questions. Neeche sirf woh exchanges include kiye gaye hain jo genuinely valuable ya r elatable hain.

Sangat member (Mahotsav ki yaad karte hue): भैया आशाएं का महा हवन का हैंगओवर हो गया है। मैं तो बहुत िडप�ेस्ड हो गया था गांव जाके। सही में भैया बहुत मुि�कल था उधर से आने का। एक्चुअली वहां से आते टाइम ना रोना आ रहा था।
Bhaiya: सही बात है, सही बात है भैया। 20 िदन मैं सच बताऊं मुझे भी नहीं पता है 20 िदन कब िनकल गए। तुम तो रात को 3-3 बजे जाते थे, घर वाले कहने लग गए थे िक कब आओगे घर पर।

Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh ek genuinely warm, r elatable moment hai jo Mahotsav jaise collective gatherings ki emotional value ko dikhata hai — sangat aur Bhaiya dono apni nostalgia openly shar e kar rahe hain.
Sangat bhai (scheduling conflict poochte hue): भैया हम गुजराती लोग गरबा खेलने जाएंगे तो क्या करें?
Bhaiya: तुम पहले साधना करके चले जाओ यार। 40 िमनट की साधना तुम पहले करके चले जाओ। सेशन में अटेंड नहीं होगा तो चलेगा, कोई िदक्कत नहीं। िकसी भी टाइम कर सकते हैं।

Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh ek very practical, r elatable scheduling question hai jo festival season mein bahut logon ko face karni padegi, aur Bhaiya ka flexible r esponse r eassuring hai.
Sangat bahan (women's period ke baar e mein sensitive sawaal): अगर िकसी लेडीज को समस्या आ जाती है जो अभी पीिरयड्स के िदनों में चल रही है, और िजस िदन संकल्प होगा उस िदन वो िनयम से बाहर होगी तो?

Bhaiya: अगर उस िदन आप गहन तत्व में पहले से हैं तो कोई प�भाव नहीं पड़ेगा, क्योंिक गहन तत्व का आशीव�द यही है िक �ान तत्व में 24 घंटे जाप करने के िलए दो दूत आपको असाइन होते हैं। पर अगर नहीं है तो मैं सजेस्ट करूंगा िक आप उस िदन मत ही करें, खामखा आपके ऊपर िकसी प�कार का आक्रमण हो सकता है।

Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh ek sensitive, practical guidance hai jo dir ectly kai practitioners ke liye r elevant ho sakta hai, aur Bhaiya ne isko r espectfully aur clearly explain kiya.
Sangat member (extra jaap ke baar e mein poochte hue): अगर आपने बोला िक जाप करने की जरूरत नहीं है उन नौ िदनों में, लेिकन अगर िफर भी जाप िकया जाए तो क्या इससे कुछ नुकसान होगा?

Bhaiya: नुकसान नहीं होगा, आप जाप कर सकते हो। पर हम िसफ� इतना ही कहते हैं िक यह साधना करो, मोर देन इनफ है। बहुत ज्यादा मंत्र जाप से शरीर के अंदर घबराहट आने लगती है — रोम रोम कांपने लगता है। अगर आप कर सकते हो, आपके पास िहम्मत है, तो आप कीिजए।
Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh ek important safety-r elated clarification hai — "mor e is not always better" ka teaching, jo naye practitioners ke liye especially useful hai.
